transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Noah Patel (Redwood CSM), Ari Chen (Fluxware Head of ML), Priya Rao (Fluxware Cloud Infra), Sam Ortiz (Fluxware Finance), Lena Park (Fluxware SRE)

Summary (auto): discussed May usage spike, cost delta from estimate, tail latency regressions, and next steps for pilot scale.

[00:00] Jordan: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to run through the mid year stability and cost sync, figure out where the May spike came from and then align on the pilot expansion timeline.
[01:10] Ari: yeah thanks. quick context — we saw a big uptick May 12 through 18, about 3x our baseline. most of that was autocomplete calls for the new composer feature. not sure if caching was bypassed because of prompt variance.
[02:05] Priya: there were also a couple of deployment churn events on our side, kube restarts, that might have pushed bursts while requests retried to the hosted endpoint.
[03:00] Maya: okay that maps — when retries hit the host we saw regen attempts and prefix cache misses. sometimes the kv cache key shaping means small prompt token changes break the cache, so throughput drops and unit cost rises.
[03:42] Lena: we did see error 429s during the window then fallback to the lower tier model — logging shows retries.
[04:20] Jordan: to be explicit, you were on Redwood hosted API at that time, not Dedicated, correct?
[04:27] Ari: correct, still hosted. pilot was planned for dedicated but not enabled yet.
[05:10] Sam: finance question — our May bill was ~42% over forecast. which levers do we have short-term to bring that down? quantization, batching, or switch to dedicated?
[06:00] Maya: short-term we can tune batching and introduce more aggressive prefix caching. mid-term quantization profiles can drop token cost significantly but needs validation on quality. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and often better unit economics at scale, but there's commit level to consider.
[06:48] Priya: on committed capacity, what's the smallest band we can pilot with? we don't want to over-commit if usage normalizes.
[07:20] Jordan: we typically recommend a small dedicated pool with burst capacity — e.g., 1-2k tokens/sec sustained with scheduled autoscale. we can propose a 3-month pilot with a break clause. I'll send a pricing tier.
[08:05] Ari: latency — we've been tracking p95/p99 and the p99 in June is creeping up to 780ms from 540ms baseline. p50 is almost unchanged.
[08:50] Maya: that suggests tail queuing or GPU context switch overhead on some batches. could be model variant fallback or garbage collection on host nodes. we'll want to correlate the trace ids. can your team share a sample of traces?
[09:30] Ari: yes we can share. Priya will pull a 24-hour sample around the peak.
[10:00] Priya: noted, we'll export traces and the corresponding request IDs. also, we have SSO changes planned next week — might affect calls if token exchange changes.
[10:40] Jordan: good to note. security/compliance — you had specific asks last cycle around KMS and audit logs. where are we on that?
[11:10] Sam: finance/legal still wants to see SOC2 and the KMS flow end-to-end — especially for PII redaction.
[11:50] Noah: Redwood's security pack includes SOC2 report, ISO docs, and KMS integration guide. we'll push an updated pack with the HSM/KMS flow, but note private deployments (VPC/on-prem) give you customer-managed keys if that's needed.
[12:35] Ari: we might require bring-your-own-key for the pilot, or at minimum, an explicit KMS integration test.
[13:05] Jordan: we can include that in the pilot acceptance criteria.
[13:50] Maya: on the technical side, for the benchmark we suggest three scenarios: baseline traffic (your production distribution), spike simulation (3x for 1 hour), and long-tail test to reproduce p99. we'll capture token cost and latency percentiles.
[14:40] Priya: how intrusive is that run? can we do it on our staging with a mirror?
[15:05] Maya: staging mirror is ideal. if you can't mirror we can run in dedicated test pool with your prompt set; results should be comparable.
[15:45] Ari: we also want to validate output quality after quantization — some of our scoring is sensitive to small probability shifts.
[16:20] Maya: absolutely. quantization profiles are model-dependent; we do a regression suite against your prompts and we can flag quality regressions.
[17:05] Sam: for finance forecasting: when you say quantization saves X%, can you give a ballpark?
[17:30] Jordan: rough numbers: 8-bit quant can reduce model memory and cost per token by ~20-35% depending on model and throughput pattern. caching + batching often has bigger wins for chatty workloads.
[18:10] Lena: on the ops side, SLOs — can Redwood expose per-route token breakdowns? we'd like per-endpoint cost and latency visibility.
[18:40] Noah: yes, the console exposes token-level breakdowns and per-model/per-route latency. we can add a custom dashboard for your top routes.
[19:05] Priya: good. we want the trail for audit: request IDs, payload hashes, and redaction logs — can those be exported?
[19:30] Noah: audit logs are exportable to your SIEM; data retention windows are configurable on Dedicated/Private. HOSTED has a standard retention policy, but we can discuss enterprise retention add-on.
[20:10] Jordan: timeline question: if pilot runs in July, when could you be in dedicated?
[20:30] Ari: we prefer to start pilot by early July and have an internal decision by mid-August.
[20:45] Jordan: that's achievable — 3-week ramp for the pilot, plus the benchmark next week.
[21:20] Maya: technical note: when you move to dedicated, warm KV cache import helps a lot. if you can provide the most common prompts, we can pre-seed cache to reduce tail misses.
[22:05] Priya: will do.
[22:30] Ari: any red flags on regulatory — we operate in EU + US and a few privacy constraints for EU PII.
[22:55] Noah: Redwood supports regional routing; we can pin inference to EU regions and integrate with your KMS in that region as well.
[23:30] Sam: about the uptick: is there an interface-level mitigation to prevent future sudden spend if a new client feature causes bursty usage? can we set per-route caps?
[24:10] Jordan: yes, there are rate-limits and quotas per API key and per-route. also automatic fallback to a smaller variant if the cost reaches a threshold can be configured.
[25:00] Maya: note fallback can affect quality; we should implement alerts + an automated grace window rather than instantaneous fallback.
[25:40] Priya: what about autoscaling aggressiveness? if we set very conservative autoscale you avoid overprovisioning but risk queueing.
[26:10] Maya: it's a tradeoff. we can tune the autoscale policy to prioritize latency SLOs during business hours and cost outside peak.
[27:00] Ari: on roadmap, we plan to roll a new Summarization model next quarter. how disruptive are model rollouts for caching and latency?
[27:25] Maya: rollouts can invalidate caches depending on model changes. we recommend canary rollouts, A/B with traffic split, and automatic rollback if quality or latency regress. Redwood has rollout tooling to orchestrate that.
[28:10] Lena: can you give example rollback thresholds?
[28:30] Maya: default is p99 latency +5% and quality delta of -2% on your evals; but we can tune thresholds per route.
[29:00] Sam: finance again — Jordan, you'll send updated pricing that models the 3-month pilot, dedicated cost, and projected token savings from caching/quantization?
[29:25] Jordan: yes, I'll send a proposal with scenarios.
[30:05] Ari: for the benchmark, Priya will provide traffic distribution and the top 20 prompts. Priya?
[30:15] Priya: yes I'll upload by Friday (2027-06-17).
[31:00] Jordan: recap next steps: security pack, benchmark, pricing. anything missing?
[31:20] Ari: include a short doc on how to pre-seed KV cache and the tradeoffs.
[31:40] Maya: will attach a short runbook for cache seeding.
[32:05] Noah: I'll create the CRM entry and schedule the follow-up on June 25 for post-benchmark review.
[32:45] Sam: one more: competitor question — internal self-host vs Redwood dedicated — what's the main ops delta?
[33:10] Maya: main delta is in orchestration and maintenance. self-hosting requires significant infra expertise: kernel tuning, dist-batching, and model kernel optimization. Redwood's Dedicated abstracts that and provides autoscale and rollback tooling. plus the observability stack and SLO tooling.
[34:05] Ari: noted.
[34:30] Jordan: quick note — we'll include SOC2 snapshot and the KMS integration guide by Friday.
[34:50] Priya: thanks.
[35:10] Maya: technical ask — can Fluxware agree on one canonical eval set for quality regression tests? that'll make rollouts and quantization validation meaningful.
[35:45] Ari: yes, we'll pick 200 representative prompts and an automated metric.
[36:20] Jordan: anything else from finance?
[36:40] Sam: no, just please include the break clause language in the pilot pricing.
[37:05] Jordan: will do.
[37:30] Priya: ops — can Redwood provide a dashboard demo of per-route token breakdown in the next call?
[37:55] Noah: yes, we'll demo that and include a shared dashboard.
[38:20] Ari: last item — auditability for PII redaction: how do you surface redaction logs and can we get attestations?
[38:50] Noah: we can surface redaction events at per-request level and provide attestations as part of the compliance pack. for full attestations we'd need enterprise agreement.
[39:25] Lena: fine, we'll review.
[40:00] Jordan: ok final recap: Redwood will share security pack (SOC2 + KMS guide), Maya will run the dedicated benchmark with Fluxware prompts, Jordan will send pricing for 3-month pilot with break clause, Fluxware will provide traces and top prompts by 2027-06-17, and Finance will review projections by 2027-06-21.
[41:10] Ari: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[41:30] Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up in CRM and schedule the next review for after the benchmark.

End of transcript.
